walkthroughs.body_html:
Design For Manufacture & Project Management — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Design For Manufacture & Project Management brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Design For Manufacture & Project Management.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is a tolerance on an engineering drawing?
options: The allowable variation in a dimension
The hardness of the specified material
The expected lifespan of the product
The cost limit for the component

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a jig?
options: To guide a tool or hold work so repeated operations are identical
To measure surface finish
To display the project schedule
To store finished components safely

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes QA from QC?
options: QA is the system preventing defects; QC inspects outputs against the specification
QA happens after sale; QC happens before design
QA tests prototypes; QC writes the design brief
QA and QC are identical activities

mcqs.q: Why do manufacturers use standardised bought-in components such as hinges?
options: They are cheaper and more reliable than making equivalents in-house
They make every product look unique
They avoid the need for quality checks
They are required for all products by law

mcqs.q: Why do manufacturers use jigs and fixtures?
options: Jigs are only needed for one-off craft products made by hand.
Overlapping bars show tasks that have gone over budget.
They locate the work and guide tools so each repeated operation is identical, giving batch accuracy and speed without marking out every individual part.
A jig is the rotating chuck that grips work in a lathe.

mcqs.q: Does design for manufacture mean making a product as advanced as possible?
options: No — it means simplifying for production: fewer parts, standard components, processes matched to the production scale, reducing cost, time and assembly errors.
DFM means packing in advanced features to impress customers.
DFM is a law requiring products to be made in the country of sale.
A jig is the rotating chuck that grips work in a lathe.

mcqs.q: On a Gantt chart, what do overlapping bars show?
options: Tasks scheduled to run concurrently — in parallel — which shortens the overall project compared with doing every task in sequence.
DFM is a law requiring products to be made in the country of sale.
Tasks on a Gantt chart must always run one after another, so bars never overlap.
Overlapping bars show tasks that have gone over budget.
